The SAFE method integrates individual fielding performance against positional averages, weighted by ball-in-play frequency and run consequences. It uses logistic curves to model success probability as a function of distance, capturing the continuous nature of fielding. The method assumes that fielding success is a smooth function of spatial proximity and direction, and that deviations from average performance can be quantified in terms of expected runs saved. Hierarchical shrinkage addresses small-sample bias by borrowing strength across players. The core insight is that fielding performance is not discrete but continuous, requiring probabilistic modeling to capture nuanced contributions to team outcomes.
